question.text: Which statement best reflects regulatory authority over commodity derivatives trading?

answer.text: SEBI has jurisdiction over commodity derivatives markets and can suspend stock exchange business or prohibit undesirable speculation under SCRA; the Government formulates the permitted commodity list
Only the Central Government regulates commodity derivatives markets
Once a commodity is listed, no authority can restrict its trading
Only exchanges can decide to stop trading in a commodity

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI regulates commodity derivatives markets. Under the SCRA, SEBI has powers including suspending stock exchange business and prohibiting undesirable speculation. The Government formulates the list of commodities permitted for derivatives trading. The Trap: Authority is shared — SEBI exercises market-regulator powers under SCRA while the Government controls the permitted commodity list. Exchanges also have some powers but operate under SEBI oversight. Note: Frame interventions in terms of SCRA powers (suspension of business, prohibition of undesirable speculation) and the Government's role in the permitted commodity list rather than general delisting language.
